phase: P5.3b (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash staged host-relayed hand-off, same-device and cross-device)
summary: Every staged DeepSeek-V4.1 run - one card (--gpus 0,0) and two cards (--gpus 0,1, stage 1 with its own weight copy) - is byte-identical to an unsplit control for all 64 greedy token ids, within this engine's measured cross-process reproducibility (unsplit twins 64/64, cross-device staged twins 64/64). Closing this witness took five root causes, each found on hardware and each gated on the host afterwards; the last was the i_widx upload missing the SWA per-query stride, which made the FIRST column-1 pass (position 64) attend rows the window table never held.

residency_equalization.why: the expert VRAM budget is computed from free VRAM after the dense half, and the shapes differ (unsplit ~23.6 GiB, staged --gpus 0,1 ~17.6 GiB on the card the budget reads), so at default budgets a staged run keeps a DIFFERENT set of experts resident than its control. Expert residency changes the tier path and with it the float summation order, which flips greedy argmax at knife-edge rows - witnessed default-budget cross-device at lcp 1/54 and default-budget same-device at 51/54 (the latter was the i_widx bug ON TOP of this). This is a performance/tier characteristic, not a state-seam property: with the budget pinned to one identical ranked head (same rank.bin seed, same cap), a staged cross-device run matched its control bitwise (probe p5.3b-dumpdiff-20261025-184223: P row bitwise, midL19 p14 x_state 0/20480 differ, 54/54 tokens).
residency_equalization.residual: with slots pinned, decode rows still differ from ~1e-1 down after the first pass because the unsplit tier prefetches ahead while staged skips prefetch (admission TIMING differs, not capacity); 54/54 tokens still agreed and every diff stayed far below the argmax margins.
